title: Smt capabilities
description: The capabilities blob of Smt.Capabilities: what a lab can know before a run. It takes no problem set. Nodes run the same module as the host (a node on another version refuses the work), so what is said here is the pool's. An application reads its limits and the words of the documents of a run here instead of carrying copies of them: every list of words is the controller's own list, the one the documents are written with. Nothing in it names a machine.

profile.description: The one pinned solver of this version: every problem of a run is solved by it, under the same numbers on every node.

id.description: The profile's id, as a run's options name it.

module.description: Where the solver module is, relative to the controller's folder.

module_sha256.description: The module's pinned SHA-256: a module with other bytes is not compiled.

module_present.description: The host's copy of the controller has the module with the pinned bytes.

engine.description: The WebAssembly engine the module runs on, with the version of its native library.

queries.description: What can be asked of a problem.

defaults.description: What applies when a run's options leave a value unset (0 means unset, the sampling rate aside).

rlimit.description: The solver's resource limit of one check: the profile's number.

hard_cap_s.description: Seconds of a reference machine for one problem, turned into fuel at time.fuel_per_second.

memory_mb.description: The solver's own memory ceiling of one problem.

sampling_rate.description: The share of the packages solved on two machines, rounded up to a whole package: any rate above 0 solves one package twice at least, so a set of one package is solved twice whole.

ceilings.description: The most a run's options may ask for; a run whose options pass one is refused.

time.description: How the budgets relate to time. Both budgets of a session are counts: the solver's resource limit of a check, and fuel, which the hard cap is turned into at fuel_per_second. The wall clock gives no verdict: a node keeps a backstop of its own, backstop_base_ms and backstop_slowdown times the time the fuel takes at the reference rate, and a session the backstop ends is a fault of the node.

session.description: What one session of the solver may write and keep.

output_bytes.description: Everything a session may write, its models included; the write that passes it ends the session as output_exceeded.

transcript_bytes.description: The end of a session's transcript a row keeps.

message_characters.description: The most characters of a row's message.

memory_headroom_bytes.description: The least the host's cap of the solver's linear memory stands above the solver's own ceiling.

problem.description: The ceilings of one submitted problem; a problem past one is refused with its code.

problem_set.description: The ceilings of a problem set (JSON lines, one problem a row).

results.description: The words a row of the results of SmtRun may say (smt-results.schema.json), each list the controller's own, and the codes of a package a node could not work on at all. A field of a row says one word of its list, or the empty word where the results schema allows it (settled_by without an answer, the code where the status says it all, validation_reason where the class says it all).

statuses.description: status: the statuses of a row of the results. A node's fault is never one (its problem goes out again); the server's no_result and disputed are.

codes.description: code, by the status of the row: the code of a refused row (the refusal codes of the problem set and the sanitizer, also the keys of the report's refused_by_code), the kind of a crash of the solver, what the nodes said last of a problem left without a result (also the keys of the integrity document's no_result_by_reason), and the outcome of a dispute that stands. Every other status has the empty code.

reasons.description: reason: why a check has no verdict or an enumeration is not complete.

expected.description: expected: the verdict the row or the problem's :status expects.

expected_agreements.description: expected_agreement (also the keys of the report's expected).

validations.description: validation: what the server's evaluator said of the row's models and values.

validation_reasons.description: validation_reason of a partial or a failed class (also the keys of the report's partial_by_reason): the evaluator's codes, output_exceeded for a model that did not come whole, and budget_package for a row whose result package had used up what the server's evaluator spends on one package.

settled_by.description: settled_by: how the answer was settled.

node_faults.description: The codes of a package a node could not work on at all (the keys of the integrity document's node_faults_by_code).

run.description: The words of the report and the integrity document of SmtRun beside those of a row, each list the controller's own.

sampling.description: sampling: whether the sampling that was asked for happened.

bindings.description: binding: whether the platform told the server which package each result came back for.

rounds.description: The round of a fan-out of the integrity document.

repair_reasons.description: The keys of the integrity document's repairs_by_reason: the words of a problem without an answer (results.codes.no_result), and copies_short.

rejected.description: Why the server refused a result package (the keys of the integrity document's rejected).

stopped_by.description: The budget that stopped a problem of the report's long tail as unknown; the empty word when none did.

packages.description: What one package a node is sent may hold.

node.description: What a node runs a package with: one session a core, at most max_degree, as many as ram_headroom of its available memory holds at session_bytes a session (twice the host's cap of the solver's linear memory under the default options, and session_margin_bytes), at the priority below normal; and the least memory a machine has for the planner to send it a package (min_ram_mb).

min_ram_mb.description: The least memory of a machine, in MiB of the total its node reports, for the planner to send it a package: the requirement the activity that solves a package declares. It stands for a machine sold as 8 GB, which reports a little less than 8,192 MiB of the memory its system sees. A 6 GB machine, below it, does not hold one session at the default options in ram_headroom of what it has available while its client and its system run. The planner admits a node that has reported no capabilities; such a node refuses a package it has no memory for (memory_insufficient), and the repair round sends its problems out again. Written since controller 0.4.0; absent in the documents of earlier versions.

benchmark_unit.description: The unit of the pool's rate: problems of the reference set a second.

platforms.description: The platforms a node runs the controller on.

pool.description: The pool a run submitted now would be planned on, as totals; absent when the host cannot say. The nodes are those the server would plan the activity that solves a package on, with its requirements applied: a machine below node.min_ram_mb is not counted, a node that has reported no capabilities is (the planner admits it). No node is named.

nodes.description: Nodes that hold the controller and meet the requirements of the activity that solves a package, for this submitter now.

workers.description: Sessions at once of the measured nodes, added up; absent when the host does not carry every measured node's degree.
